Rashi on Megillah 18b:10:1.hebrew: דקא מסדר פסוקא - על פה וכתב ליה, וקתני יצא ע"י קריאת אותו סידור:
Rashi on Megillah 18b:10:1.english: That he was reciting a verse - by heart and writing it down, and [yet the Mishnah] teaches [that] he fulfilled [his obligation] through reading that recitation:

Rashi on Megillah 18b:11:1.hebrew: הלכה כדברי האומר כולה - צריך לקרות, ופליגי בה תנאי במתני': "מהיכן קורא אדם את המגילה ויוצא בה ידי חובתו? רבי מאיר אומר: כולה, ר' יהודה אומר: מאיש יהודי":
Rashi on Megillah 18b:11:1.english: The halakha is in accordance with the statement of the one who says all of it - [Meaning one] must read [all of it], and Tannaim disagree about this in the Mishnah: "From where does a person read the Megillah and fulfill his obligation with it? Rabbi Meir says: All of it; Rabbi Yehuda says: From 'There was a certain Jew'":

Rashi on Megillah 18b:12:1.english: That a Megillah is lying before him - and he is copying from it:

Rashi on Megillah 18b:12:2.hebrew: מסייע ליה לרבה - מתני' דקתני יצא וליכא לאוקמה אלא במעתיק מן הכתב, מסייע ליה לרבה:
Rashi on Megillah 18b:12:2.english: Supports Rabbah - The Mishnah, which teaches "he has fulfilled [his obligation]" and can only be established [as referring] to one who copies from a written [text], supports Rabbah:

Rashi on Megillah 18b:12:3.hebrew: דלמא דאיתרמי ליה - לעולם מותר לכתוב בלא העתק, ומתני' דאתרמי ליה מגילה ומעתיק ממנה, ואיצטריך לאשמעינן דהיכא דמעתיק ממנה, אם כוון לבו יצא:
Rashi on Megillah 18b:12:3.english: Perhaps [it is a case] where it happened [to be before] him - Actually, it is permitted to write [a Megillah] without a written copy, and the Mishnah [is speaking of a case] where a Megillah happened to be [available] to him and he is copying from it; and it was necessary to teach us that where he is copying from it, if he directed his heart [to fulfill the obligation], he has fulfilled [his obligation]:

Rashi on Megillah 18b:14:1.hebrew: התעיף עיניך בו ואיננו - אם תכפול עיניך ממנה, הרי היא משתכחת ממך כהרף עין:
Rashi on Megillah 18b:14:1.english: Will you glance upon it fleetingly with your eyes? It is already gone - If you avert your eyes from it [the Torah], it is forgotten by you in the blink of an eye:

Rashi on Megillah 18b:16:1.hebrew: דבי בר חבו - מוכר תפילין הוה, כדאמרינן בבבא מציעא (דף כט:): "תפילין דבי בר חבו שכיחי":
Rashi on Megillah 18b:16:1.english: The house of Bar Chavu - He was a seller of tefillin, as we say in Bava Metzia (29b): "The tefillin of the house of Bar Chavu are common":

Rashi on Megillah 18b:17:1.english: And the halakha [is], etc. - Thus [is] a halakha [given] to Moses from Sinai:

Rashi on Megillah 18b:17:2.english: They are memorized - [They are] fluent in everyone's mouth:

Rashi on Megillah 18b:18:1.hebrew: סמא - זרניך בלשון קודש, אורפומניט"ו בלעז:
Rashi on Megillah 18b:18:1.english: Samma - [It is] zarnikh [arsenic] in the Holy Tongue [Hebrew], orpiment in Old French:

Rashi on Megillah 18b:18:2.english: Sikreta - [It is] a red paint with which they color shields:

Rashi on Megillah 18b:1:1.hebrew: סירוסין - למפרע, כמו "סרס את המקרא ודרשהו", וכן "יצא מחותך או מסורס" (נדה דף כח.):
Rashi on Megillah 18b:1:1.english: Out of order - Backwards, as in "Transpose [sares] the verse and expound it," and similarly, "[if it] emerged cut up or disarranged [mesoras]" (Niddah 28a):

Rashi on Megillah 18b:4:1.english: [Who] takes into consideration an individual [opinion] - In a case where the individual is stringent and the majority are lenient:

Rashi on Megillah 18b:4:2.hebrew: שומרת יבם - מצפה ליבמה, ומצוה בגדול ליבם; בא אחד מן האחין וקידש את אחותה של יבמה, אחר שנפלה היבמה לפניהן:
Rashi on Megillah 18b:4:2.english: [A woman] waiting for a levir - [She is] waiting for her brother-in-law, and the mitzvah is upon the oldest [brother] to perform levirate marriage. One of the brothers came and betrothed the sister of the widow [awaiting levirate marriage], after the widow had fallen before them [for levirate obligation]:

Rashi on Megillah 18b:4:3.english: We say to him: Wait - from marrying her:

Rashi on Megillah 18b:4:4.hebrew: עד שיעשה אחיך הגדול מעשה - ביבמתו, או לחלוץ או ליבם. אבל בעוד היבמה לפני כולן לחלוץ או לייבם, הרי היא לכל אחד כאשתו על ידי זיקת יבום, ואסור באחותה משום אחות אשה, דקסבר: יש זיקה אפי' בתרי, וכל שכן בחד. ופליגי רבנן עליה ואמרי: הואיל ושני אחים הן, אין זיקתו מיוחדת להיות מוטלת על אחד מהן להיות כאשתו, ומותר באחותה:
Rashi on Megillah 18b:4:4.english: Until your older brother acts - with his yevamah [deceased brother's widow], either to perform chalitzah or to perform yibbum [levirate marriage]. However, as long as the yevamah stands before all of them for chalitzah or for yibbum, she is [considered] like the wife of each one by virtue of the zikah [levirate bond] of yibbum, and he is forbidden [to marry] her sister because of [the prohibition of] a wife's sister, for he [Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira] holds that zikah applies even with two [brothers], and all the more so with one. And the Sages disagree with him and say: Since there are two brothers, his zikah is not specifically assigned to rest upon any one of them to be [considered] like his wife, and [therefore] he is permitted [to marry] her sister.

Rashi on Megillah 18b:6:1.english: Omitted - The scribe skipped a verse in it, and the reader read them:

Rashi on Megillah 18b:6:2.english: Like a translator who translates - by heart:

Rashi on Megillah 18b:9:2.english: To return a reasoned [answer] - something that comes from the understanding of the heart:

Tosafot on Megillah 18b:17:1.hebrew: תפלין אינן צריכין שרטוט - פירש ר"ת דכן הלכה:
Tosafot on Megillah 18b:17:1.english: Phylacteries do not require scoring - Rabbeinu Tam explained that such is the halakha:

Tosafot on Megillah 18b:4:1.hebrew: נקוט דרב ביבי בידך - דאמר רב: אין הלכה כרבי מונא, שאמר שחוזר לראש; וכן הלכה, דאין צריך לחזור לראש, דהלכה כרב באיסורי דאמר כן. ורבי יוחנן קאי כוותיה בפרק בתרא דר"ה (דף לד: ושם), דאמר: שאם שמע תשע תקיעות בתשע שעות ביום — יצא. ומסיים התם: תניא נמי הכי, ומייתי הא; ופריך: והא אמר רבי יוחנן משום ר"ש בן יהוצדק שאם שהה כדי לגמור את כולה חוזר לראש? ומשני: הא דידיה, הא דרביה. ומדתניא כוותיה, שמע מינה הלכתא כוותיה. ומכאן סומך ר"י, כשעומד ב"אמת ויציב", שממתין עד שיאמר עם הצבור קדושה וברכו ואמן יהא שמיה רבא:
Tosafot on Megillah 18b:4:1.english: Grasp [the version of] Rav Beivai in your hand - For Rav said: The halakha is not in accordance with Rabbi Mona, who said that one returns to the beginning; and so is the halakha, that one does not need to return to the beginning, for the halakha follows Rav in ritual matters [issurei], who said so. And Rabbi Yoḥanan stands in agreement with him in the last chapter of Rosh Hashanah (34b and there [in the parallel]), where he says that if one heard nine shofar blasts during nine hours of the day, he has fulfilled his obligation. And [the Gemara] concludes there: "It was also taught thus [in a baraita]," and it brings this [ruling]; and it asks: "But didn't Rabbi Yoḥanan say in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak that if one paused long enough to complete the whole [recitation], he returns to the beginning?" And it answers: "This [statement] is his own, while that [statement] is his teacher's." And since it was taught [in a baraita] in accordance with him, learn from this that the halakha is in accordance with him. And on this basis, Rabbeinu Yitzḥak relies [on this ruling] when he is standing in "Emet veYatziv," [holding] that he may wait until he says Kedusha, Barekhu, and "Amen, yehei shemei rabba" with the congregation:

Tosafot on Megillah 18b:4:2.hebrew: שקידש אחיו את אחותה - דווקא קידש אומרים לו "המתן" מלישא, דכיון דאינה עדיין אלא ארוסה, נראה שנושא אחות זקוקתו; אבל אם נשאה, אשתו גמורה היא ואין צריך להמתין, דהא פקע זיקה לגמרי. ודוקא קידש אחר נפילה, אבל קודם נפילה, שלא היתה אחות זקוקתו בשעת הקדושין, אין אומרים לו "המתן", שהרי לא היתה שום זיקה מעולם. וטעמא דר' יהודה, משום דסבר יש זיקה:
Tosafot on Megillah 18b:4:2.english: Whose brother betrothed her sister - Specifically [when] he betrothed [her], they say to him, "Wait" from marrying [her]; for since she is still only a betrothed woman, it appears as though he is marrying the sister of [a woman] bound to him [by the levirate bond]. But if he [already] married her, she is his full-fledged wife and he does not need to wait, for the levirate bond has completely lapsed. And specifically [when] he betrothed [her] after [her] falling [into levirate obligation]; but before [her] falling, when she was not the sister of [a woman] bound to him at the time of the betrothal, they do not say to him, "Wait," for there was never any levirate bond [at that time]. And the reason of Rabbi Yehuda [ben Beteira] is because he holds [that] there is a levirate bond:
